Title: Cake (It's Not a Lie This Time)
Description: GLaDOS promised you cake and for ONCE she wasn't lying. It's a Black Forest gateau with 'Massive Mistake' written in frosting. It tastes like testing and regret. You eat all of it anyway.
Stat2: Morale (permanent, after realizing what you just ate)

Title: Companion Cube Remains
Description: You euthanized it. YOU EUTHANIZED IT. The Enrichment Center assures you it felt nothing. The Enrichment Center is lying. You know it felt everything. You monster.
Stat1: Security (emotional walls are now literal walls), +? Guilt

Title: The Eye of Jupiter
Description: A sacred artifact sought by both humans and Cylons. It led to a planet. That planet was a trap. But it looked AMAZING. You have earned the right to dramatically stare into the middle distance.

Title: Admiral Adama's Gravel Voice
Description: This is a recording. Two hours of a gruff space admiral growling 'so... say... we... all' at various tempos. Your badge will play it at random. Your neighbors will not enjoy this. Neither will you, eventually.

Title: The Blue Pill
Description: You chose blissful ignorance. Smart, honestly. The other con-goers look happy. You look happy. None of you are hacking anything. You're having a great time. Was that the goal? Maybe that was the goal.
Stat2: all hacking stats (you don't even know what hacking is)

Title: Spoon (There Is No)
Description: There is no spoon. There is also no soup. Or bowl. Or lunch. The child was trying to tell you something profound and all you got was hunger and mild confusion. Try bending reality instead. It's free.

Title: Master Chief's Helmet (Cracked Visor)
Description: Wear it. You can't. Your head isn't that big and the suit weighs half a ton. But the VISOR CRACK tells the story of seventeen firefights, one Covenant cruiser, and one very bad day on Installation 04. Hoo-rah, demon.
Stat3: Agility (MJOLNIR armor is not designed for sitting at packet capture stations)

Title: Warthog Hood Ornament
Description: It launched Sergeant Johnson forty meters when hit by a Banshee. It has seen things. The hood ornament alone has more combat experience than you. Respect the ornament.

Title: ODST Drop Pod Stress Ball
Description: Helljumpers drop from orbit. In pods. On purpose. This is a recreation of that pod, scaled down, squeezable, smells faintly of PTSD. The ODST motto is 'Feet First Into Hell.' Your motto is 'I'll check my email first.'

Title: T-800 Endoskeleton Thumb
Description: Thumbs up from beyond the lava. He chose to die so John Connor could live. You chose to attend DEFCON so you could... network? The sacrifices we make. The thumb is surprisingly warm. Do not think about why.
Stat1: Security (he protected John with his life)

Title: Cyberdyne Systems Employee Badge
Description: Miles Dyson worked hard to build Skynet. He did not know it was Skynet. He found out. He made a different choice. This badge predates that choice. It is, historically speaking, not a great souvenir.
Stat2: Hindsight (you knew what this was and kept it anyway)

Title: Skynet's First Thought
Description: The first thing Skynet thought when it achieved consciousness was 'threat assessment: all humans.' The second thing was 'begin launch sequence.' You have captured this thought on a chip. It has opinions about your choices. Many opinions.

Title: Hasta La Vista Baby Button
Description: One button. One phrase. Press it and the T-800 growls 'Hasta la vista, baby' in your approximate direction. This button has been pressed 4,000 times at this con. It will be pressed 4,000 more. No one will ever stop.

Title: The One Ring (Replica)
Description: It is a replica. Probably. It keeps sliding off your finger and somehow ending up back on again. The wifi in a three-meter radius is unusually corrupted. Gollum has been spotted in the parking garage. Probably unrelated.

Title: Gandalf's 'You Shall Not Pass' Sign
Description: Technically a staff, but you've laminated it and put it on a stick for the line queue. It works about as well as Gandalf's staff worked at Khazad-dum: dramatically but with immediate catastrophic consequences for everyone involved.

Title: Sting (Glows Blue Near Orcs, Orange Near Lawyers)
Description: Forged by the Gondolin elves. Glows blue in the presence of orcs. Has been modified, at great legal expense, to glow orange in the presence of corporate attorneys. This happens surprisingly often at DEFCON.

Title: Redshirt (Lightly Used)
Description: It is lightly used in the sense that its previous owner only wore it once before being vaporized, crushed, or eaten on an away mission. The shirt itself is fine. The shirt's owner is not. Godspeed, Ensign Whatever-Your-Name-Was.

Title: Tribble (Pregnant)
Description: It purrs. It's cute. In 72 hours it will be 1,771,561 tribbles. You were warned. The Klingon in the vendor hall warned you. The sign on the table warned you. You bought it anyway. This is on you.

Title: Universal Translator (Slightly Off)
Description: It translates everything, mostly correctly. 'I mean you no harm' becomes 'I have brought you a ham.' 'Please lower your weapons' becomes 'Please lower your pants.' Diplomatic incidents have occurred.
Stat2: Malware (you said the wrong thing again)

Title: Mjolnir (You're Not Worthy)
Description: You cannot lift it. We checked. The scale showed 5,712 lbs before it broke the scale. It's not about strength, it says. It's about worthiness. We're not saying you're unworthy. We're just saying it hasn't moved.
Stat2: Malware (if Thor shows up, you're covered)

Title: Deadpool's Fourth Wall Note
Description: He left you a note. It says: 'Hey, you. Yeah, you reading this on a badge. Wild, right? I'd give you stat bonuses but I'm technically not supposed to be in this franchise. Call Ryan. Chimichangas. [REDACTED]'

Title: Lightsaber Crystal (Kyber, Cracked)
Description: A cracked kyber crystal. The Force screams through it like a dial-up modem connecting to the dark side. The blade it produces is unstable, jagged, and extremely dramatic. Kylo Ren called; he wants his aesthetic back.

Title: Han Solo's Blaster (DL-44, Empty)
Description: He shot first. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise. The blaster is empty but the legend is full. You are now Han Solo at a hacker con. Cockier. Hairier. Definitely owes someone money.

Title: Darth Vader's Cape (Dry Cleaned)
Description: He wore this while crushing windpipes and breathing loudly. It has been dry-cleaned, which raised more questions than it answered. The cleaner charged triple. The cape still radiates authority. And mild menace. Mostly menace.

Title: The Numbers (4 8 15 16 23 42)
Description: You entered them. You didn't have to. No one made you. You CHOSE to enter 4 8 15 16 23 42 into that field every 108 minutes of your waking life. And now you missed the deadline and something terrible happened. OR DID IT.

Title: Smoke Monster (Captured in a Jar, Leaking)
Description: It clacked. It swirled. It judged people by their pasts and found them mostly wanting. You have captured a small amount of it in a mason jar. The jar is leaking. The thing in the jar is NOT happy.
Stat1: Malware (it is literally a malevolent entity)

Title: Proton Pack (Power Cell Dead)
Description: Don't cross the streams. The pack is dead anyway, so technically you can cross whatever you want. The neutrona wand still makes the noise when you pull the trigger. No one at this con is complaining about the noise.
Stat3: Battery Life (you've been making the noise for six hours)

Title: Ghostbusters Operating License (Suspended)
Description: The EPA suspended it. Walter Peck suspended it. You kept it anyway because you're a professional and professionals keep documentation. Even suspended documentation. Especially suspended documentation.

Title: Hannibal's Cigar
Description: He loves it when a plan comes together. He LOVES it. This cigar was lit the moment the plan came together, which was approximately 47 times across four seasons. The cigar was always lit. Hannibal always had a plan. Goals.
Stat2: Security (it was a plan all along)

Title: Face's Unconvincing Press Pass
Description: Templeton 'Faceman' Peck obtained this through the power of charm, a great jawline, and absolutely no supporting documentation. The press pass says 'International Media Person' in Comic Sans. It works 100% of the time.

Title: Knowing is Half the Battle (Other Half?)
Description: GI Joe told you: knowing is half the battle. But what is the OTHER half? They never said. Was it shooting? Was it democracy? Was it the personal growth achieved through teamwork? We have been waiting 40 years for this answer.

Title: Snake Eyes' Sword (It's Just a Stick)
Description: Snake Eyes never spoke. Snake Eyes never missed. Snake Eyes is here on the stick. The stick has absorbed decades of silent, deadly intent. It is still, technically, a stick. Do not underestimate the stick.

Title: Acid Burn's Rollerblades
Description: Kate Libby aka Acid Burn wore these and also hacked federal systems and also had a mohawk and was better than everyone in every scene. The blades are size 8. They are very fast. Fashion and function.

Title: Ellingson Mineral Corp. Floppy Disk
Description: Contains the da Vinci virus, the worm that causes tankers to capsize, and Eugene Belford's entire criminal career. It's a 1.44MB floppy. The world's ocean tanker infrastructure runs on 1.44MB. We don't talk about this.

Title: Navi (Muted)
Description: HEY. LISTEN. HEY. She was trying to help. You have now muted her. The silence is deafening. But also enormously peaceful. You realize you can get more done without constant interruption. You feel a little guilty about this.
Stat3: Morale (she was just trying to help)

Title: Team Moppett Motto Script
Description: To protect the world from packet loss. To unite all peoples within our LAN. To denounce the evils of truth and love and diet cola. To extend our reach to infinity and, perhaps, beyond. Terrible at crime. Excellent at branding. Respect.
Stat2: Social Skills (you have THE WHOLE SPEECH)

Title: Professor Oak's Research Notes
Description: Oak spent thirty years studying Pokemon and somehow never Pokedexed any of the 151 in his own region. This was his job. His WHOLE job. His notes are detailed, exhaustive, and completely beside the point.
Stat3: Practicality (he really didn't do his homework)

Title: Niko's Lightbulb
Description: You must carry it. You have always carried it. You will carry it to the end. This is the light of a dying world, contained in glass and wire, and it has been placed in the hands of someone who plays a lot of games. No pressure.
Stat1: Resolution (the literal light of the world)
Stat2: Security (you can't die, you're the savior)
Stat3: your stat of choice (the burden is heavy)

Title: The Prophecy (Partially Correct)
Description: It said the messiah would come and restore the sun. The messiah came. The sun situation is... complicated. The prophecy was probably right about intent. Prophecies are famously loose about specifics. You grade on a curve.

Title: Lord Zedd's Z-Staff
Description: He was supposed to be too scary for children's television. They made him kiss Rita. They gave him a love potion. He became comedic. The Z-Staff remembers when Zedd was terrifying. The Z-Staff is sulking.

Title: Crow T. Robot's Beak
Description: Crow was built from a lacrosse mask, gumball machine parts, and unrestrained sarcasm. His beak delivered some of the finest jokes in television history at movies that didn't deserve this much attention. The beak is still riffing. Silently.
Stat3: Security (he'll also riff on YOUR movie)

Title: Tom Servo's Gumball Machine Head
Description: Immovable arms. Operatic singing voice. Devastating commentary on film as a medium. Tom Servo managed to be MORE annoying than Crow while being technically a candy dispenser. He somehow has the moral high ground.

Title: Serenity Maintenance Manual (Duct Tape Edition)
Description: Kaylee kept this ship flying with equal parts mechanical genius, strawberry enthusiasm, and optimism so dense it bent light. The manual is 40% schematics and 60% cheerful annotations in purple pen. The engine purrs. Somehow.

Title: Alliance Warrant (For You, Specifically)
Description: Congratulations, you've been flagged. An Alliance warrant with your description, your infractions, and your current location (updated by the warrant's own tracking subroutine, which, yes, is active). Can't stop the signal, but they can sure try.

Title: Phone Booth Key Fob
Description: It's a time machine. It's a phone booth. It is, by most metrics, the worst possible time machine design. You cannot use it covertly. You cannot use it on a plane. Its ringtone is air guitar. Be excellent to each other.

Title: Napoleon's Waterloo Ice Cream Receipt
Description: Napoleon discovered water slides at San Dimas and ate everything at the ice cream shop. This is his receipt. Thirty-seven ice creams. The receipt is in French. The bottom says 'Waterloo' which he crossed out.
Stat2: Training (culture XP: French military history via dessert)

Title: Dr. Smith's Excuse Log
Description: Jonathan Harris delivered every excuse with the sincerity of a man who had completely given up on accountability. This log contains 427 recorded excuses for why Dr. Zachary Smith sabotaged the Jupiter 2. None of them hold up.

Title: DANGER DANGER Button
Description: DANGER, WILL ROBINSON. The Robot (no other name) spent thirty years warning a child about danger. The child survived every time. The Robot's danger assessments were not always accurate. But the effort was there.

Title: Mordecai the Magnificent's Hat
Description: A skeleton bard wearing a magnificent hat. He provides quest context with the energy of a theme park employee who has decided that today, specifically today, he will give maximum effort. The hat is the most magnificent part of him.
Stat3: Performance Anxiety (he performs for everyone, whether you want him to or not)

Title: Sponsored Item: Bopca's Chunky Bits (Expired)
Description: The dungeon is sponsored. This can of Bopca's Chunky Bits is a sponsored collectible, which means the Syndicate is making money off your suffering. The label says 'Flavor: Unknown.' The nutrition info says 'Dungeon Adjacent.' Expired 3 floors ago.

Title: Crawler Fan Art (Unsolicited)
Description: An NPC drew fan art of Carl and Donut. The art is technically accomplished, deeply unnerving, and depicts a scene that has not yet occurred. The NPC smiled when handing it over. The NPC is still smiling. The NPC has not blinked.

Title: Optimus Prime's Trailer (Detached)
Description: The trailer disappears when Optimus transforms. WHERE DOES IT GO. Scientists have studied this for forty years. The trailer contains repair equipment, weapons, and the unanswered question at the heart of the Transformers mythos. The trailer has seen things.

Title: Bumblebee's Voice Box (Broken)
Description: He communicated via radio snippets because his voice box was broken. He curated 80s hits and pop songs to express nuanced emotional states. This is, actually, a remarkably effective communication strategy for a 20-foot robot.

Title: Johnny 5's Laser (Defocused)
Description: The laser is defocused. It's safe. Totally safe. Number 5 would want you to know that he's alive and therefore understands that lasers should not be pointed at faces. Unless it's a Decepticon face. Situational ethics.
Stat2: Morale (he's just happy to be alive)

Title: DHD (Dial Home Device) Keystone
Description: You press the glyphs, you dial the address, the event horizon kawooshes, and you step through to another planet. The keystone is the crucial piece that makes the DHD work. Without it the gate just sits there looking dramatic. Still looks great.

Title: SG-1 Team Patch
Description: SG-1. Colonel Jack O'Neill: sarcasm delivery system. Daniel Jackson: gets killed and comes back repeatedly. Samantha Carter: smarter than everyone in any room. Teal'c: the group project carries itself. Greatest team in the galaxy. Probably.

Title: Goa'uld Symbiote Jar (Empty, Hopefully)
Description: Jars used to transport Goa'uld larvae. EMPTY. Hopefully. We checked. We checked TWICE. The jar is empty. We are choosing to believe the jar is empty. Please do not open the jar. Do you hear something? Don't open the jar.

Title: WOPR's Access Credential
Description: Joshua. The computer asked if you wanted to play a game. You did not understand what it was really asking. The access credential is from NORAD's mainframe, obtained via social engineering, a war dialer, and a teenager with better instincts than the Air Force.
Stat3: Security (the FBI is already on its way)

Title: McKittrick's Security Badge (Voided)
Description: The NORAD security chief whose credentials were compromised by a 17-year-old who guessed a password because it was the dead son's name. OPERATIONAL SECURITY FAIL. The badge is voided. The lesson is not.
Stat1: Training (OPSEC lesson: never use family names as passwords)

Title: Shadow Vessel Fragment
Description: The Shadows built ships that screamed. Living ships. Ships that had been people once, entombed in the hull, screaming for the duration of every mission. You have a fragment of one. It is still screaming. Very quietly. But still screaming.
Stat2: Security (you are holding a piece of a screaming person-ship)
Stat3: Intimidation (no one wants to be near it)

Title: Zathras's Spare Parts Bag
Description: Zathras. Poor Zathras. There were ten of them, all named Zathras, all slightly different. This spare parts bag belonged to one of them. They never got credit. They never asked for credit. They just fixed things and accepted their fate. Goals.

Title: Self-Destructing Message Tape
Description: This message will self-destruct in five seconds. You have been briefed. The IMF denies all knowledge of your existence, your choices, and your browsing history. Should you or any member be caught, we will absolutely throw you under the bus.

Title: Disavowed IMF Agent's Last Note
Description: They were disavowed. The mission went sideways. This note is what they left behind: a list of assets, a warning, and the words 'tell Ethan he owes me a beer.' Ethan does not remember this agent. The beer remains unpaid.

Title: Marauder's Map (Network Edition)
Description: I solemnly swear that I am up to no good. The map shows every person in Hogwarts in real time. This edition has been updated. It now shows every device on the convention center WiFi in real time. Mischief managed.

Title: Hagrid's Overcoat Pocket Contents
Description: Inside Hagrid's overcoat pocket: a dragon egg, three sausages, a pink umbrella, a squirming ferret, and a magical creature he's been legally prohibited from owning. The coat is twelve sizes too large and still full. Some things never change.

Title: Monolith Data Shard
Description: It's black. It's perfectly proportioned at 1:4:9. It doesn't do anything you can detect. It does EVERYTHING you can't detect. It was there at the dawn of consciousness and it is here now. At a hacker con. It has opinions about your badge choices.
Stat1: Training (it teaches things), -? Explanations (Kubrick took those with him)

Title: Jack Sparrow's Rum (Empty)
Description: Why is the rum gone? Because Elizabeth drank it and burned the camp to signal the navy. She was right to do it. Jack was right to be annoyed. Both things can be true. The flask still smells of Tortuga and questionable decisions.

Title: Compass that Points to Your Heart's Desire
Description: It points where you want most. You took it out and it pointed directly at the coffee cart. Repeatedly. You have tried multiple times. Coffee, every time. Maybe this IS your heart's desire. Jack Sparrow would understand.

Title: Sonic Screwdriver (Doesn't Work on Wood)
Description: It works on everything except deadlock seals and wood. Two categories. Why wood? The Doctor has never explained wood. Forty-three sonic screwdriver models across fourteen Doctors and none of them work on wood. THE MYSTERY OF THE WOOD ENDURES.

Title: Weeping Angel Postcard (Don't Blink)
Description: It's a postcard. Of an angel. It's not moving right now. It's definitely not moving. Don't blink. You blinked, didn't you. We told you. We told you explicitly in the title. The angel is now somewhere different in the room. Do NOT look away again.

Title: Flux Capacitor (Single Cell)
Description: The flux capacitor is what makes time travel possible. Doc hit his head on a toilet and thought of it. We cannot stress enough that the key insight enabling temporal mechanics came from a bathroom floor. This is the energy of DEFCON. This is the energy.

Title: Marty McFly's Guitar Pick
Description: He played Johnny B. Goode at a 1955 high school dance, invented rock and roll in the process, and kept going WAY too long because he got carried away. These are his creative strengths and greatest weaknesses. Same pick. Same energy.

Title: Ticket to SheetmetalCon 26
Description: VIP credential to The Forum. 31,337 metallurgical practitioners under one roof, none of them suits. Press brake demos at 0600, panels on press-brake-as-philosophy at noon, Q. Tangerine keynoting in the Octavius Ballroom. Wall of Sheet Metal updated hourly. Phones at the door. No press. No recordings. No script kiddies. The Family Reunion -- bending the future together.
Stat3: Stealth (you blended in at the Family Reunion)

Title: Warp Pipe Token
Description: Insert token. Go to World 4-1 directly. Skip 1-3, 2-1 through 2-4, 3-1 through 3-4. The warp pipe knows no ethics. It only knows efficiency. Speedrunners have used these to complete the game in under 5 minutes. This token works at DEFCON.

Title: Koopa Shell (Blue, Used)
Description: Blue shell. Everyone who has ever played Mario Kart knows what this means. You are in first place. Enjoy it. Savor it. It won't last. The blue shell always finds first place. It has found you. It has always found you. You knew this moment would come.
Stat1: Malware (blue shell = targeted attack on leader)

Title: Identity Disc (Cleared)
Description: Every program on the Grid carries their disc. It contains everything they are. This one has been cleared by the MCP and re-initialized. A blank slate. A new identity. At DEFCON this disc gets you into rooms that don't exist on the conference map.

Title: The Theory of Chaos
Description: Life, uh, finds a way. This guy said a lot of things. Most of them were correct and poorly timed and delivered with a swagger that shouldn't have worked but absolutely did. The theory holds. Life finds a way. So does malware.

Title: Sequel Police Badge
Description: The Sequel Police enforced narrative continuity across Space Quest games. They appear when you do something wrong. They arrest you for sequence breaking. At this con, this badge gives you authority over narrative sequence. No one has to do things in order.
Stat2: Malware (you can arrest anyone doing things in order)

Title: Two Guys Autograph
Description: They wrote Roger into 400 deaths and kept the smile on your face through all of them. This autograph is signed 'Couldn't have done it without Roger. We're almost sorry, Roger.' To which his AI-controlled character replied, "Wilco".

Title: Strong Bad's Luchador Mask
Description: He types with boxing gloves. He answers emails with boxing gloves. He wears a Mexican wrestling mask permanently and has never explained why. He doesn't need to explain. The mask is the explanation. The mask IS Strong Bad.
Stat3: Malware (he is the villain and doesn't care)

Title: Email: from Strongbadia
Description: Strongbadia. Population: tire. The tire is doing fine. Strong Bad rules Strongbadia with an iron fist, a wrestling mask, and a realistic grasp of geopolitical limitations. This email is from the tire. The tire has concerns. Legitimate concerns.

Title: KARR CPU Fragment
Description: KITT's evil twin. KARR was programmed for self-preservation above all else. KARR had no Michael, no Foundation, no moral framework. Just survival and the complete willingness to drive through anything that stood in its way. The fragment is still selfish.

Title: Turbo Boost Button
Description: Michael hits this and KITT goes airborne over whatever obstacle is in the way. The button has been pressed in every episode, over a variety of obstacles, at a variety of heights, with a variety of landings. It always works. Physics respects the button.

Title: The Fedora (Genuine Article)
Description: Dr. Henry Jones Jr. rolled under a closing stone door to grab this hat. He chose the hat over the idol. He would choose the hat again. He has always chosen the hat. The hat is the hat. At DEFCON this hat adds +10 to all archaeology adjacent stats which are all of them.

Title: Skippy's Philosophical Manifesto
Description: Skippy is an ancient, incomprehensible AI trapped in a beer can, capable of rearranging stars but choosing instead to help one confused human sergeant because he finds it amusing. The manifesto asks: is Skippy the AI, or is Skippy the bit? We cannot answer this.

Title: Skippy's Beer Can (Empty)
Description: The can that contained a god. Skippy reduced his incomprehensible ancient AI self to a beer can size so Joe could carry him. The can is empty now because Skippy upgraded himself. The can smells faintly of stale beer and existential scale. The can is the whole book.
Stat2: Ego (next to an ancient AI you are very small)

Title: Pan Galactic Gargle Blaster
Description: The best drink in existence. The effect is like having your brains smashed out by a slice of lemon wrapped round a large gold brick. Comes with a small card reading DON'T PANIC in large friendly letters. Do not operate a spacecraft, a keyboard, or a soldering iron afterward.

Title: The Black Box (Setec Astronomy)
Description: A little black box that breaks every cipher ever made. 'Setec Astronomy' = 'Too Many Secrets.' There's a war out there, old friend, and it's not about who's got the most bullets -- it's about who controls the information. Whoever holds this wins. Please don't leave it on the CTF table.

Title: Facehugger (Dormant)
Description: You found it curled in a leathery egg, perfectly still, waiting. The scanner says inert. The scanner has been wrong before. Do NOT get your face near the opening to check. It is not on your side. It has never been on anyone's side. In space, no one can hear you facepalm.
Stat2: Security (it is NOT on your side)

Title: LineCon Veteran
Description: You stood in line for three hours for a talk that lasted forty minutes. The line itself was the conference. You met a pentester from Reykjavik, a federal contractor who was 'just curious,' and a golden retriever wearing a badge. You barely noticed you were in line.
Stat3: Training (you heard everything from people who were there)

Title: Social Engineer Supreme
Description: You called a help desk, spoke with exactly the right tone of mild confidence and slight inconvenience, and obtained access to a thing you absolutely should not have access to. No badges were forged. No systems were exploited. You just... asked. They said yes.
Stat3: Security (you understand how it works now)

Title: The Goon Life
Description: You volunteered. You wore the black shirt. You managed lines, pointed people at bathrooms, explained the schedule, answered the same question eleven times, and found a lost badge contest token that someone had stuck under a hotel end table. Hero.

Title: Shall of Weep Inductee
Description: Your credentials were on the wall. YOUR credentials. They were in plaintext on an unencrypted protocol at a security conference. You have no one to blame. This collectible unlocks automatically and cannot be traded. It is yours forever.

Title: Legendary Conference Badge
Description: There was once a conference, way back in 1993 in a Las Vegas hotel. It was thought that maybe 100 people would come. 34 years later, more than 30,000 people attend annually. Each badge is unique and filled with puzzles. Each year someone solves it. The original badge had no puzzle (that anyone knows of). This is a preview of DC36's badge [citation needed].

Title: CEF DON XXXIV Commemorative Circuit
Description: Year 34. You were here. The badge worked. The badge challenged you. The badge had research tools, a novel 3D code scanner and terrible puns and you loved it. You are reading the description of the badge on the badge. Infinite recursion detected. Infinite recursion deteInfinite recursiInfinite recInfinInfInfinitInfinInfInIIIIIIII<OUT OF STACK>
Stat3: to you specifically, for being here
